sentences.text: Briefly stated, the factual matrix of the case as averred in the plaint is that plaintiff is a banking company under the Banking Regulation Act 1949 and the defendant is a borrower.

It is further stated that on 18.09.2020, the defendant opted for Guaranteed Emergency Credit Line (GECL) by way of Working Capital Term Loan Facility of Rs.2,14,717/- against the security of a commercial vehicle 'EICHER PRO 1075' which was already hypothecated by defendant in favour of plaintiff bank against the existing loan account no. LVNOD00041160849.
It is further stated that the defendant executed various documents for the Working Capital Term Loan in favour of the plaintiff bank on 18.09.2020.

It is further stated that the plaintiff sanctioned the said Guaranteed Emergency Credit Line (GECL) by way of Working Capital Term Loan Facility of Rs.2,14,717/- vide sanction letter dated 18.09.2020 and that the defendant agreed and accepted the terms of the said loan facility and also signed the said sanction letter.

It is further stated that pursuant to signing the said sanction letter, the defendant accepted the terms of the loan facility and the plaintiff disbursed an amount of Rs.2,14,095/- to the account of the defendant under loan account no. UVNOD00042088345 against the security of a commercial vehicle 'EICHER PRO 1075' after deducting disbursement charges in terms of the loan documents.
3. It is further stated that the said Working Capital Term Loan was disbursed on applicable interest/fixed rate of interest @ 9.25% p.a. which was chargeable on the principal amount of the loan facility.

It is further stated that the tenure of the loan facility was 4 years from the date of disbursement and the defendant was provided moratorium of 12 months on principal amount during which interest would continue to UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSH JOSHI Date:
2025.01.10 17:31:04 +05'30 accrue and become payable during the moratorium period.
It is further stated that the principal amount was to be repaid in 36 EMIs after expiry of moratorium period.

It is further stated that pursuant to the receipt of the loan, the defendant committed defaults in repayment of loan amount and did not adhere with payment schedule and that the defendant failed to pay the installments despite various reminders sent by the plaintiff.

It is further stated that the plaintiff had already filed a civil suit for recovery against the defendant on 23.01.2023 bearing no.
CS (Comm) 154/2023 respect to the existing loan account no. LVNOD00041160849 which was listed before the court of Ld. DJ, Commercial, Central, THC, Delhi wherein the said court had allowed the application under Order 40 CPC Rule 1 read with Section 151 CPC and appointed a bank officer as a receiver to take possession of the commercial vehicle 'EICHER PRO 1075' which was already hypothecated by defendant in favour of plaintiff bank against the existing loan account no.
LVNOD00041160849.
4.

entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: It is further stated that defendant has also defaulted in payment of installments of the present loan account no. UVNOD00042088345 qua which the present suit has been filed.

It is further stated that defendant in terms of the loan documents executed had paid an amount of Rs.67,776/-
i.e. the interest during the moratorium period for first 12 months out of 48 EMI + 4 EMI after the expiry of moratorium period and had defaulted in repayment of Rs.47,971/- i.e. 29 EMIs after the expiry of moratorium period and Rs. 13,449 towards late payment and cheque bouncing charges total amounting to Rs.61,420/- besides future installments of Rs.1,50,764/- against the loan account no. UVNOD00042088345 as on 29.11.2022.

It is further stated that since UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.01.10 17:31:12 +05'30' there was default in repayment of the monthly installments, the plaintiff bank in terms of the loan documents executed by the defendant,
Icici Bank vs Rahul Singh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16132154/
2 recalled the loan facility available to the defendant by way of sending a loan recall notice dated 29.10.2022 but despite the receipt of the notice, the defendant did not repay the outstanding amount.

It is further stated that as per the loan account maintained by the plaintiff, an amount of Rs.1,99,605/- is payable by the defendant towards principal, penal interest and other dues as on 29.11.2022.

Therefore, the present suit has been filed by the plaintiff seeking the relief as mentioned in paragraph no.1.
5.
Summons issued to the defendant by way of publication were received back served on 05.02.2024.
However, despite due service of summons, no one appeared on behalf of defendant and neither any written statement was filed by the defendant.
Accordingly, the right of defendant to file written statement was closed and defendant was proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 08.05.2024.
6. Thereafter, the matter was listed for ex-parte evidence of the plaintiff.
It is pertinent to mention that the present suit was instituted by the plaintiff through its authorised representative (hereinafter referred as AR) namely Mr. Shaurya Jaiswal.
However, Mr. Sunil Chaudhri was substituted as the new AR of the plaintiff vide order dated 07.08.2024 pursuant to an application for substitution of AR filed by the plaintiff.
7. In order to prove its case, the AR of plaintiff namely Mr. Sunil Chaudhri stepped into the witness box and was examined as PW-1.

PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A and relied upon the following documents:
 UMANG Digital  UMANG J  JOSHI Date: 2  17:31:2  i. Power of Attorney Ex. PW1/1 (OSR).
 ii. Sanction letter Ex. PW1/2.
iii. Undertaking in relation to security Ex. PW1/3. iv. ECLGS for MSMEs- Self undertaking by borrower Ex. PW1/4. v. Copy of the loan recall notice Ex. PW1/5 (colly).
 vi.
Postal receipts Mark X (colly).

vii. Certified copy of the statement of account Ex.PW1/6 (colly).
viii. Certificate u/s. 2A of Bankers Book of Evidence, 1891 Act Ex. PW1/7.
ix. Certificate u/s 65-B of the Indian Evidence Act Ex. PW1/8.
8.
However, despite giving an opportunity for cross-examination of PW-1, the same was not availed by the defendant as the defendant remained ex-parte.
Thereafter, AR of plaintiff closed plaintiff evidence vide statement dated 07.08.2024 and the matter was listed for final arguments.
At the stage of final arguments also, no one appeared on behalf of defendant and accordingly, ex-parte final arguments were heard.

sentences.text: Ex-parte final arguments heard.
Record perused thoroughly.
10.It is pertinent to mention that PW-1 namely Mr. Sunil Chaudhri has deposed on the lines of the pleadings.
Perusal of power of attorney Ex. PW1/1 (OSR) denotes that the said witness has been duly authorised by plaintiff company to prosecute the present matter against the defendant.

Furthermore, the sanction letter Ex. PW1/2, undertaking in relation to security Ex. PW1/3 and ECLGS for MSMEs- Self undertaking by borrower Ex. PW1/4 corroborates the plea of the UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.01.10 17:31:27 +05'30' plaintiff that the plaintiff had sanctioned the Guaranteed Emergency Credit Line (GECL) by way of Working Capital Term Loan Facility of Rs.2,14,717/- to the defendant and that the said loan amount was to be repaid by the defendant being the borrower.

11.It is pertinent to mention that the statement of account dated 29.11.2022 Ex. PW-1/6 (colly)
maintained by the plaintiff in respect of the loan account of the defendant bearing no.
UVNOD00042088345 shows that an amount of Rs. 1,77,480/- is the principal outstanding amount due to be paid by the defendant to the plaintiff.

Furthermore, Ex. PW-1/6 (colly) mentions the total amount payable by the defendant as Rs. 1,99,605/- which is inclusive of the principal outstanding amount of Rs. 1,77,480/- along with late payment penalty, cheque bouncing charges, interest for the month, prepayment charges and interest on pending installment.

12.However, the plaintiff has failed to show the basis for computation of the aforesaid late payment penalty, cheque bouncing charges, interest for the month, prepayment charges and interest on pending installment.

Therefore, in view of the above, this court is not inclined to award the amount being claimed by the plaintiff from the defendant as late payment penalty, cheque bouncing charges,
prepayment charges and interest on pending installment.
13.Be that as it may, the documents relied upon the plaintiff have remained unrebutted and uncontroverted in view of no reply and no cross-examination by the defendant.
The defendant has failed to discredit the version of the plaintiff as no written statement was filed by the defendant despite sufficient opportunity.
Furthermore, there is no UMANG Digitally signed by UMANG JOSHI JOSHI Date: 2025.01.10 17:31:43 +05'30' reason on record to discredit the unrebutted testimony of PW-1.

It was for the defendant to dispute the contractual relationship with the plaintiff or to dispute the genuineness and correctness of the loan documents or the statement of accounts or to establish that outstanding amount claimed or part thereof has already been paid to the plaintiff.
Needless to mention, defendant has failed to do so.

14.Furthermore, the suit is well within the limitation period as the same has been filed within three years from the date when the last payment was made by defendant as reflected in the statement of account Ex. PW-1/6 (colly) maintained by the plaintiff.

Furthermore, this court has the territorial jurisdiction to try the suit as part cause of action has arisen within the jurisdiction of this court as has been established from the unrebutted testimony of PW-1.
Accordingly, the plaintiff has duly discharged its burden of proof and successfully proved its case on the scale of balance of probabilities.

4 15.The
plaintiff has also prayed for interest @ 9.25 % per annum.
However, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, the court is only inclined to grant simple interest @ 9% per annum.

16.Accordingly, the present suit is hereby decreed in favour of the plaintiff and against the defendant as follows:
a) The defendant shall pay a sum of Rs. 1,77,480/- to the plaintiff along with simple interest @ 9% per annum from the date of filing of suit till realisation of the decreetal amount.
b) Cost of the suit shall be paid by defendant to the plaintiff as per rules.
 UMANG Digital  UMANG J  JOSHI Date: 2  17:31:5  17.Decree sheet be prepared accordingly.
18.File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
